Fix Linear ticket COR-2210 in the entire-brain repo (you are in an isolated worktree of it). Follow the repo's CLAUDE.md / .entire/agent-guide.md workflow (Brain brief preflight etc.).

## Ticket: factsync/publish HTTP errors double the status text ("403 Forbidden: Forbidden") (Low)

Observed (hosted sync, proposals, and sync --memories-backend=http error paths):
```
factsync: POST facts:upsert 01SBX…: unexpected status 403 Forbidden: Forbidden; pull-only
factsync: GET proposals 01KWZ…/branch: 404 Not Found: not found
publish_failed: unexpected server response (HTTP 404): not found
```
Problem: the status line already names the status ("403 Forbidden"), then the response body ("Forbidden" / "not found") is appended verbatim, doubling it. This applies wherever the shared factsync/publish HTTP error wrapper renders a response.

Expected: render the status once; append the body only when it adds information beyond the status text (e.g. a real server detail like "pull-only" should stay).

## Approach notes
- The factsync side: `internal/factsync/` — there is an `h.detail(resp)` helper (see httpproposals.go) that appends the body; `internal/factsync/error_body_test.go` pins current behavior. Fix the dedup in the shared detail/rendering helper, case-insensitively: suppress the body when it equals (or is contained in) the status text after trimming; keep bodies that carry extra info (the "; pull-only" suffix pattern must survive — note the server may return "Forbidden; pull-only" as one body: strip only the redundant leading status echo, keep the rest).
- The publish side: grep `unexpected server response (HTTP` for the publish error path and apply the same rule.
- Recent relevant work: COR-2204 (merged) made proposals `list` swallow queue-unsupported errors; your change affects the text INSIDE remaining errors — safe, but run the facts/proposals/publish test files to be sure.
- Update the tests that pin the doubled text; add cases for: body == status text (suppressed), body with extra detail (kept, deduped prefix), empty body.
- Keep scoped to internal/factsync + the publish error rendering; avoid internal/cli/add.go, connect, distill, privacy files (parallel agents own those).

## Workflow requirements
1. `git fetch origin main` and create your branch from `origin/main`: `git checkout -b cor-2210-http-status-dedup origin/main`.
2. Minimal change, repo idiom (comments explain WHY only).
3. Run `gofmt -l -s` on changed files (must be empty), the focused factsync/cli tests, plus one full `go test ./... -count=1` (must pass).
4. Commit with explicit file names (never `git add -A`). End the commit message with:
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
5. Push the branch (a first push may be transiently rejected — retry once). Create the PR: `gh pr create --base main` with a cold-reader body (Why / What changed / Validation), ending with:
🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
6. Do NOT touch Linear; the parent session handles it.

Report back: PR URL, 3-5 bullets, before/after examples of each error shape, validation run, any risks.

a relationship question.

committed-tree results as analysis of edits they do not contain.

Ask per-symbol commands before bulk streams. Never dump unfiltered whole-repo

inspection. State unresolved coverage limits in the answer.

Both sets of mandatory rules apply.
Brain answers recorded-context and historical questions; Graph answers structural
questions and entity-level revision comparisons.

They NEVER replace required neighbors or impact analysis.
Graph results NEVER replace required retrieval of prior decisions or attempts.

location; it NEVER exempts relationship questions from Graph or historical
questions from Brain. Small edits, follow-ups, read-only reconnaissance, specs,

an answered question in source is not verification.

a reproduction, or the most relevant build. If execution is unavailable, disclose
that limit and perform a bounded source check. Prefer precise queries and line ranges,
but never trade resolution for fewer turns.

Current source and executed tests establish present behavior. Historical memory

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Render the HTTP status once in factsync/publish errors (COR-2210)

A server whose error body echoes the status text had it rendered twice,
because every call site prints the status and then appends the body
verbatim: "unexpected status 403 Forbidden: Forbidden; pull-only",
"unexpected server response (HTTP 404): not found".

httpx.StripStatusEcho now drops a body that says no more than the status
line and cuts a leading echo from one that says more ("Forbidden;
pull-only" keeps "pull-only"). ErrorDetail applies it, covering factsync
and hostedbrain; the publish path pre-reads its body, so
publishServerDetail passes the status code and strips directly. Matching
is exact and ASCII-case-insensitive — near-miss spellings such as
nginx's "504 Gateway Time-out" are kept.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && git push -u origin cor-2210-http-status-dedup
